commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Bond
commitResults.messageBody: Update the Java entry point, startup banner, and documentation so the project consistently uses the new chatbot name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add initial Bond greeting and farewell
commitResults.messageBody: Display the chatbot banner, greet the user, and exit with a farewell message as required.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command echo and bye handling
Add task storing capability and list command
Add task completion status with mark command
Task data changed to  Task class
Move Java classes into bond package
commitResults.messageBody:
The Java classes use the default package, which does not follow the
project's coding standard and makes the source structure unclear.

Move Bond and Task into the bond package and align their Javadocs
with the SE-EDU Java conventions without changing chatbot behavior.

Java changes need a consistent, project-specific interpretation of
the SE-EDU basic and intermediate coding rules.

Add a reusable skill with the applicable rules and require agents to
load it whenever they create, edit, refactor, or review Java code.

Commit and branch conventions need to remain consistent across future
agent work.

Add a reusable skill for SE-EDU Git rules and require agents to load it
when preparing commits or branch names. Preserve explicit authorization
for committing and pushing.

Keep generic tasks available while introducing Todo as a separate task type.

This provides the first Level 4 increment before applying inheritance.

Let users create time-sensitive missions.

Keep dates and times as strings for this incremental implementation.

Let users record missions that occur during a specified time period.

Keep event dates and times as strings for this incremental implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task types to use inheritance
commitResults.messageBody:
Todo, Deadline, and Event repeat common task behavior.

Reuse Task as their parent so each subtype only handles its own details.

Add a reusable project skill and test plan for checking console
commands against their expected output.

Require agents to review the plan and run the UI tests after code
changes so user-visible regressions are caught promptly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bond: Extract command handling from main
commitResults.messageBody:
Bond's main method handles startup, command selection, input parsing,
task mutation, and response rendering in one place. Readers must track
several responsibilities and abstraction levels through a long method.

Extract the session loop and command-specific operations into focused
helper methods. Keep main at the lifecycle level so the program flow is
clear, while each command's existing parsing and output stay together.

This preserves observable behavior while making future command changes
easier to locate, understand, and review.

Todo, deadline, and event commands repeat the same storage, counting,
pluralization, and confirmation-output logic. Keeping those copies in
sync makes later changes harder and creates avoidable inconsistency risk.

Route all three task types through one helper after their command-specific
fields have been parsed. This retains the distinct parsing logic while
keeping the shared addition workflow in one place.

The refactoring preserves all command behavior and console output.

Command recognition uses string literals while argument extraction relies
on matching numeric offsets. A prefix change can therefore leave parsing
silently out of sync with command detection.

Define each command prefix once and derive argument boundaries from the
selected prefix's length. This makes the relationship explicit and removes
unexplained substring positions without changing the command grammar.

The refactoring preserves all existing input and output behavior.

Bond passes a task array and a separate count through its command
handlers. Those values describe one collection but can be changed or
passed independently, making invalid combinations possible.

Introduce TaskList to own the array, size, capacity, insertion, and
lookup operations. Update Bond to depend on that abstraction instead of
managing the collection representation itself.

Add the new source file to the documented UI-test build command. Console
behavior remains unchanged and all UI cases continue to pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bond: Separate UI and command parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Bond still owns console rendering and command interpretation alongside
application control. This mixes responsibilities and forces changes to
input syntax or output wording through the central coordinator.

Introduce Ui for console interaction, Parser for command recognition and
argument conversion, and CommandType for explicit dispatch. Keep Bond
focused on coordinating parsed operations with the task list.

Update the documented build command for the new source files. The change
preserves existing commands and output, verified by every UI test case.

Task exposes its description and completion state to every subclass even
though none requires direct field access. This widens the mutation surface
and makes the class responsible for fewer of its own invariants.

Make both fields private and make the description final because it does
not change after construction. Continue exposing completion changes only
through the existing mark and unmark operations.

This tightens encapsulation without changing task behavior or output.
